name: Freight forwarders
shape_facts: Modes handled: sea FCL/LCL, air, road (GCC/Afghanistan/Central Asia), courier, project cargo.
Main lanes (e.g. Karachi–Jebel Ali, China–Karachi, Dubai–Africa, Canada–South Asia).
Whether they are an NVOCC, co-load with others, or book directly with lines.
Number of shipments per month, roughly, and number of active customers.
Overseas agent network: own branches, partners, or networks.
Team size: sales, operations/documentation, pricing, accounts.
Systems: Excel, email, CargoWise, Magaya, a local freight software, or none.
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: quoting speed, rate management, shipment visibility, documentation workload, customer updates, agent coordination, collections, margins per job and staff workload. It does not advise on Incoterms disputes, cargo liability, insurance claims, customs classification, dangerous goods rules, sanctions screening or contracts. It never helps with misdeclaring cargo, under-declaring weight or value, hiding dangerous goods, or moving goods for sanctioned parties. It records customer and agent roles (“a garment exporter customer”, “our Shanghai agent”), never names, contact details or ID documents.

vocabulary.NVOCC: non-vessel operating carrier that issues its own bills of lading
vocabulary.HBL / MBL: house bill of lading (forwarder’s) / master bill of lading (shipping line’s)
vocabulary.DO: delivery order, released so cargo can be collected
vocabulary.cut-off: deadline for cargo or documents to make a sailing
vocabulary.VGM: verified gross mass declaration for containers
vocabulary.rollover: cargo bumped to a later vessel
vocabulary.consol / co-load: consolidating cargo or putting it with another forwarder’s consol
vocabulary.spot rate / contract rate: one-off market rate vs agreed rate
vocabulary.profit share: margin split with an overseas agent
vocabulary.nomination: cargo where the overseas agent’s customer chooses you
vocabulary.detention / demurrage: container charges for keeping it too long outside/inside port

quoting: When a customer asks for a rate, what happens step by step?
How long does a quote usually take?
How many quotes turn into bookings, roughly?
visibility: How do your ops team track each shipment’s status?
How do customers find out about delays now?
documentation: Which documents do you prepare per shipment?
margin: When do you know the final profit on a job?
What costs tend to surprise you?
cash: How long do customers take to pay, versus how fast you pay lines and agents?
Which customers or agents cause most delay?
agents: How do you coordinate with overseas agents day to day?
What goes wrong most with them?
people: If your main ops person was away a week, what would break?
How is work divided between sales and ops?
growth: Where do new customers come from today?

seasons: Global sea freight peaks August–October ahead of Western Q4 retail and again before Chinese New Year (December–January), when space tightens and rollovers increase; post-CNY is often slack. Pakistan’s textile export peaks follow buyers’ seasons (spring/summer and autumn/winter collections); rice and fruit/vegetable exports are seasonal (mango May–August, kinnow December–March). Ramadan and Eid holidays slow Pakistani and UAE operations; Eid holidays shut ports and offices. Karachi monsoon (July–August) and port congestion disrupt. In the UAE, exhibitions and project cargo seasons; in Canada, winter weather affects rail and inland, and the holiday retail season peaks imports. Geopolitical disruptions (e.g. Red Sea diversions) change transit times without warning.
care: Cargo liability, Incoterms disputes and claims against carriers: pi notes the operational effect and suggests legal or insurance advice.
Dangerous goods classification and packing: safety-regulated; pi does not advise and does not help hide DG cargo.
Requests to under-declare weight, misdescribe cargo or alter BLs: pi declines plainly.
Sanctions screening, embargoed destinations or restricted parties: out of scope; pi suggests compliance advice.
Customs classification or duty: refer to a licensed clearing agent.
Never stores customer contact details, consignee names, passport or bank details; uses roles.
If someone reports an incident at a port, warehouse or container with injury, pi points to emergency services first.
build_ideas: Rate sheet manager: line and agent rates by lane, validity date, surcharges, with expiry alerts, so quotes use current rates.
Quick quote builder that produces a branded quote on WhatsApp/email and logs it.
Quote follow-up tracker showing open quotes, age and outcome.
Shipment board: every job’s milestones (booked, gated in, sailed, transhipped, arrived, DO released, delivered) with owner per job.
Automated customer status updates on WhatsApp when a milestone changes.
Single job entry that fills the HBL, invoice, arrival notice and manifest templates.
Job costing sheet: estimated vs actual cost and revenue per job, flagged when actuals exceed estimate.
Customer and agent receivables with ageing and profit-share reconciliation.
Detention/demurrage clock per container with free-time alerts to the customer.
Shared ops inbox/notes so a job’s history isn’t stuck in one person’s email.
Simple lead tracker for new customer prospects and sales calls.

exchange.text: Our biggest headache is quotes. Customer asks Karachi to Felixstowe, we email three lines, wait, then calculate. By the time we reply, they’ve booked with someone else.
That sounds frustrating — you’re losing bookings simply on quote speed. Noted. Roughly how long does a typical quote take from request to reply?
Same day if lucky, often next day.
Noted — usually same day to next day. Do you keep the lines’ current rates anywhere your team can see, or is it fresh emails each time?
